newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris -Fla. ruling not on merits.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris -Fla. ruling not on merits.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos said Friday that a ruling by a Florida judge to allow the state to pursue civil racketeering claims against the industry is not a ruling on the merits of Florida's claim but rather simply one that lets the state go ahead.
"(The ruling) is not a ruling on the merits of the state's claim, it merely permits the state to make allegations," the company said in a statement.
"Philip Morris U.S.A. firmly believes it will become clear, as this case goes forward, that the state cannot support these unfounded allegations," the company said.

"The state's asserting civil RICO is an act of desperation in response to the court's dismissal of 15 of 18 claims contained in the state's first complaint," said Gregory Little, senior assistant general counsel for Philip Morris, in the statement.
He called the state's RICO claim, which was added after the initial claim was filed, "An afterthought designed for media attention."
A spokeswoman in New York for Philip Morris said the company would have no other comment on the ruling beyond the statement.
